{{Quote|The ancient Sith called this [chain of islands and coastlines] Circle of Visions. The rest of the planet went undeveloped while they focused all their attention on five specific sites along this circle.|[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Natua Wan]], [[44 ABY]]|<ref name="FotJ:A" />}}
The '''Circle of Visions''' was a circular chain of volcanic islands and coastline locations on the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith World]] of [[Upekzar]] that ran from the planet's equatorial regions down to its south pole. The ancient [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] who colonized the planet confined their settlements to five distinct locations along the Circle of Visions, each of which hosted an extensive volcanic cave system home to colonies of [[rhak-skuri]].

==Description==
{{Quote|Volcanic caves, caverns, tubes—all formed when lava continued to flow beneath a top layer that cooled faster, forming a crust. The Sith thought these caves significant, and when they ventured to explore them, many Sith suffered hallucinations.|Natua Wan, 44 ABY|<ref name="FotJ:A" />}}
The Circle of Visions was the name applied to a circular chain of isolated islands and coastline locations found on the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith World]] of [[Upekzar]]. Stretching across the planet's southern hemisphere from its equatorial regions down to its south pole, the Circle of Visions was notable for its high concentration of volcanos and associated lava cave systems formed from retreating magma. The latter cave networks often hosted colonies of [[rhak-skuri]], a subspecies of [[diplura]] endemic to Upekzar who hunted by means of a [[Pheromone/Legends|pheromone]] known to cause nightmare-like hallucinations in certain [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species.<ref name="FotJ:A" />

The ancient [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] who settled the planet focused their colonization efforts on five main locations along the Circle of Visions. Here, abiding in settlements and cities that dwelt in the shadows of the Circle's volcanos, the Sith conducted ritualistic [[Mysteries]] in nearby cave systems, unprotected from the pheromones of the rhak-skuri. Though each settlement hosted rites related to a distinct aspect of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and could be found in locations as diverse as the south pole and the equatorial heartlands, the planet's [[Abandoned city of the Sith|largest city]] lay close to the [[High Rites cave system|expansive cave system]] associated with the [[High Rites]].<ref name="FotJ:A" />

==History==
{{Quote|[The Sith] deemed the volcanic caves special places, and conducted initiations and other rites of passage without protection from the pheromones. The caves were, if not a dark-side nexus precisely, definitely a site in which the dark side flourished. Centuries of rituals imbued with the power of fear and anguish induced by the pheromones only strengthened that...They dwelled close to the five major places where they performed their Mysteries. Each settlement was located near an elaborate lava cave system that had a specific focus.|Natua Wan, 44 ABY|<ref name="FotJ:A" />}}
The Circle of Visions was first discovered by the ancient Sith of the Sith Empire. During their initial explorations of Upekzar, the Sith discovered the Circle of Visions' volcanic cave systems and stumbled upon the native rhak-skuri, an insectoid subspecies of diplura who inhabited the volcanic caves along the Circle of Visions. These Sith explorers frequently experienced nightmare-like hallucinations mediated by means of the rhak-skuri's pheromones, and over time, the Sith residents of Upekzar came to develop and conduct a number of rituals of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] and [[Sith acolyte/Legends|acolyte]] initiation ceremonies that involved protracted exposure to the creatures' pheromones.<ref name="FotJ:A" />

The Sith restricted their colonization efforts to five major sites along the Circle of Visions, each of which hosted a settlement and cave system associated with a certain rite of their ritualistic Mysteries. The [[Cold Rites]] were conducted close at hand to Upekzar's frigid south pole, while the [[Rites of Fire]] were held in the equatorial regions of the planet. The most significant rituals, undertaken by only the most powerful Sith [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]] on the planet, were the [[High Rites]], held within an [[High Rites cave system|extensive cave system]] in one of Upekzar's more temperate locations. The planet's largest city lay some three [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] away in the shadow of a dormant volcano.<ref name="FotJ:A" />

In 44 ABY, during the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order's]] search for the Force entity [[Abeloth]] and the [[Sith Meditation Sphere]] known as [[Ship (Sith Meditation Sphere)|Ship]], [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and a strike team of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] investigated the ruins of the ancient Sith city and the extensive cave system in which the Sith had performed their High Rites. While spelunking through the latter, [[Ben Skywalker]], [[Vestara Khai]], and Natua Wan discovered that as a result of the residual dark side energy generated by centuries of Sith rites, the rhak-skuri had mutated into two-meter-tall creatures that had evolved some degree of [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]]. These creatures were able to recognize Khai as a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathically]] communicate with her, and differentiate between [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light-sided]] and dark-sided Force users.<ref name="FotJ:A" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Circle of Visions makes its sole [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] appearance in ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]'', and is only mentioned by name once in the novel's text despite serving as the setting of the Upekzar-based narrative section.
